requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace and the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
rationale:
I judged the supplied tests adequate for `requirements.examples.definition`. I read only the supplied test sources and requested no implementation source. Each obligation maps to tests as follows.

- **Fence syntax (at least three colons, closing fence at least as long, MAY define).**
  - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]` opens examples with 4 and 6 colons and closes them with 5 and 7.
  - The same test puts a nested 3-colon `{note}` fence inside the body. That checks a shorter fence does not close the example.
  - The default 3-colon form appears in most other tests, including `fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` in `src/lib.rs`.
  - An unclosed example is reported ("missing a closing colon fence") in `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[example_errors_include_duplicates_invalid_bodies_and_missing_tests]`.
- **Name uses the chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules.**
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` registers `requirements.something.foo` from `requirements.md`.
  - It leaves `:::{example} bad name` literal and creates no definition for it.
  - The evidence tests derive `rules.case` from `md/rules.md`.
  - Duplicate example names are reported in the `example_errors_include_duplicates...` test.
- **Body includes all Markdown between the fences, trimmed, without option lines.**
  - `fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]` asserts `example.text` equals the body exactly. The body has a heading, nested fences and a code block, and the test surrounds it with extra whitespace.
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text]` asserts `:test:` option lines are excluded from an example body and from the rendered output.
  - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable]` asserts the example's evidence text matches without the option lines.
- **Concrete case with expected behavior.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[initial_prompt_carries_the_review_criteria]` asserts that an example's prompt carries the example task. That task begins by checking for a concrete case with expected behavior. An empty example body is also rejected ("has no text").
- **At least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference.** `fn[examples_may_reference_their_requirement_with_cite_or_test]` accepts `{test}` and `{cite}` examples. It rejects a missing reference (`nested`, which cites an example), `{impl}`, a literal or escaped reference, an unknown name, and `{term}`. The `example_errors_include_duplicates...` test also flags an example with no references.
- **`{cite}` and `{test}` direction, and using both.**
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs]` checks both directions. The cited requirement becomes an input to the citing example's assessment (`requirements.citer` gets `requirements.ready`). The testing example `requirements.tester` becomes an input to `requirements.ready`'s assessment, while the citing example `requirements.citer` does not.
  - `fn[cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates]` has an example using both roles. It validates end to end, including the evidence inputs.
- **Example directive in a fenced code block stays literal.** Both `fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]` (no `rules.literal` definition) and `fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` (`hidden` remains literal text) check this.

I found no obligation without a test that exercises it and asserts its outcome, and no marking gap. The relevant tests all carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace and the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, and needs
no evidence input. Its issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Code implementations are reviewed as part of the definitions they implement or
test. Citation reviews assess cited source items and book passages under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
